The turning point for me was when I matched my trading style with my personality. I would read one trader's journal, then I'd say I want to be a scalper, then I would read another and say I want to trade higher timeframe. While it is true, that the read on both types of charts are the same, finding what type of trader you are is important. Take a day or two and find yourself. Your chart reading is really good, you just now have to figure out what type of trading style fits your personality. It took me a while to understand that learning how to read the market is only 25% of the battle. Learning yourself and disciplining yourself to stick to what best suits you is the other 75%.

Hello Josh, i see you're quite confident in the edges of CPPAZs as holding levels, then you often trade bounces from them. You do like this because even if it breaks into CPPAZ the price will retrace, or you have always special reasons like previous engulfs in opposite direction, or others? Thanks a lot, all the best

Orders are always on the edges of any PAZ. Whether it be a FL, stacked FTRs, or CPAZ. We never trade midrange. I stopped out of this trade, but it was totally my fault. I have to continue to tell myself, "ONLY TAKE TRADES AFTER AN ENGULF." After going through many of my trades, I noticed that I only lose when I anticipate a retrace when I think price is ranging. Waiting for the engulf takes the guesswork out, and it leads us in the right direction. Yes they're orders on the edges of these PAZs, and we will get a bounce, but without an engulf, anything could happen. I just have to remind myself of that very thing.
